findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: There are observed several small holes along the wall along in the dish room above the sink basin. Maintenance was made aware and will be sealing these holes. Ensure that the holes are sealed to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: There is observed a small drip taking place at the drain pipe of the walk-in cooler unit. PIC has not food stored below that poses a contamination hazard. Maintenance has been made aware of the drip and will be making repairs on the unit. Ensure food continues to be stored away from the drip until repairs are made that prevent the drip from taking place. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The dish machine was tested and recorded at 0ppm chlorine sanitizer at the start of the inspection. Maintenance was called and is performing maintenance on the machine during the inspection. The machine had tubes replaced during today’s inspection and a cycle was ran. The machine was retested and recorded at 50ppm chlorine, operating properly. Ensure daily testing is accomplished to ensure proper sanitizer concentration.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The triple sink is observed to have pulled away form the wall on the far right corner which has created a gap that the seal is not covering. Ensure repairs are made to the sink to make it flush with the wall and creates a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 

6-501.11: The coving of the facility is observed to be degrading in its seal or starting to pull away form the wall in areas. Ensure that the coving is resealed to the wall to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-204.117: The dish washer is observed to no be dispensing sanitizer solution as the primer is not turning when primed or in use. Ensure this part gets replaced and allows the sanitizer to be dispensed according to manufacturer requirements.
4-204.117: WAREWASHING MACHINE, after adoption of Code, shall be equipped to: (A) automatically dispense detergents and SANITIZERS, (B) incorporate visual means to verify delivery of chemicals.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: The drain pipe under the garbage disposal is observed to be wedged and held up by an extra piece of piping. This drain pipe needs to be rapiers either by creating a more stable base for the pipe to sit on or the drain pipe needs to be properly attached to the disposal drain system. Ensure repairs are made in accordance with the plumbing code.
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: There are a few air vents and air return ducts that appear to have an accumulation of dust/soil residue in various locations throughout the kitchen. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent this residue and to prevent potential contamination from the air ducts.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Caulking observed to be in need of repair at the double and triple sink in the kitchen. The facility may utilize the splash guards that they used on the hand sink and in the dish area or they may use fresh caulking to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 100 ppm at sani buckets. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed both sani buckets within kitchen to measure a 100 ppm. Discussed routine changing of buckets in order to maintain a level of 200 to 400 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

Reference 6-201.11.

Observed caulk of hand sink near kitchen entrance to be coming away and the wall and sink. Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.comment:

750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

  (A) mop sink
  (B) spray hose in dish room

The blue metal shelving in the end of the dry goods storage room had chipping paint.

Sand and paint the chipping parts of the shelving.

findings.comment:

A repair person is coming to fix a leak in the dish machine and to adjust the chemical sanitizer concentration.  Chlorine sanitizer shall be dispensed at the concentration of 50 ppm.  A follow-up inspection will be done to be sure the dish machine is dispensing sanitizer at the correct rate.

findings.comment:

(B) Disposable aluminum food containers were stored food side up on a wire shelf in the dry goods storage room.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.152 - Pans of cooked rice in the walkin cooler were dated 9/28 and 9/26. Product dated 9/26 should have been discarded on 10/2, while product dated 9/28 should have been discarded on 10/4. Rice was discarded in the trash during the inspection. Ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods held at the establishment under refrigeration temperatures for longer than 24 hours must be properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. The day foods are prepared in-house (i.e. noodles, rice, cooked meats, etc.) or commercially processed products are opened (i.e. lunch meat, milk, cottage cheese, etc.) counts as day 1 and is the beginning of the 7 day time frame. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Foods cooling in walkin cooler had internal temperatures of 88F-105F (mac-n-cheese) and 94F (creamed corn). Neither pan was labeled with date or time. Cook that left at 2 was contacted by RN Administrator and asked when foods were placed in walkin cooler. Foods had allegedly been in cooler since ~12:30-12:45pm after they were pulled from the lunch line. Foods in the cooler were uncovered, but nobody was monitoring the cooling process in order to ensure rapid/proper cooling occurred. Both products were discarded in the trash during the inspection. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6 hrs. (see general comments)

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) Boxes of food were observed on the floor in the walkin freezer and dry storage room. Delivery was received the morning of 10/4/12. B) Condensation line of walkin cooler fan had a leak and water was observed dripping onto a box of soy milk below the line. The box of soy milk was moved, and a maintenance worker used food grade storage bags to cover the other crates of milk in the immediate area. Food shall be protected at all times. Store foods at least 6 inches off the floor, and do not store any products under the walkin cooler drain line. Properly store and protect foods.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) can opener blades (dried debris); B) knives/storage container; C) inside oven; D) drip guard of ice machine (mold); & D) drawer used for clean utensil storage at prep table (crumbs/debris). Properly clean and sanitize all food contact surface between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. **Can openers were placed with other soiled items in the dish area & drip guard was wiped off during the inspection**

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - A) (R) Soiled knives were observed with clean cutlery in a container next to clean pot/pan storage. Bottom inside the container was soiled with debris. B) (R) Drawer holding clean utensils in prep area had buildup of crumbs/debris in the bottom. Maintain storage containers and areas clean to protect utensils and equipment from cross contamination. Do not store soiled utensils with clean items. Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. **Knives/container were taken to dirty dish area**

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - A) Condensation drain line of walkin cooler fan had a leak. B) Handsink in dish area was slow draining. Maintenance worker tried to snake the drain to the handsink after a tie from a bread wrapper and what appeared to be plastic were removed from the drain by the inspector. A call for service was made for the handsink. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair the walkin cooler fan and dish area handsink in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - A) (R) Floor drain below 3 part sink was soiled with buildup. B) Floor drain below dish machine had buildup of debris. Clean the floor drains and floors throughout along walls/in corners daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) (R) Ceiling vent covers throughout kitchen had dust buildup. B) (R) Walls in dish area had dust buildup, especially around the handsink and related fixtures (i.e. paper towel dispenser, etc.). Clean walls and vent covers as needed to eliminate buildup of dust and other debris. C) Attached plumbing of dish machine had  black buildup on it. Clean the attached plumbing of the dish machine and other equipment daily/as needed.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750.540a - None of the employees working in the kitchen at the time of the inspection had a Food Service Sanitation Manager Certification (FSSMC). The morning cook (Larry) has his certification but left for the day at 2pm. The cook on duty for the evening has not yet been to sanitation class. RN Administrator made employees stop food prep until a cook that has FSSMC could come back for the remainder of the day. All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of FSSM. **Certified cook arrived to oversee food handling prior to conclusion of the inspection.**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) floor fan blowing in dish area (dust buildup) & B) can opener blade (dried debris). Properly clean and sanitize all food contact surface between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. **Can opener was placed with other soiled items to be taken to dish area**

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils

B) Drawer holding clean utensils in prep area had buildup of crumbs/debris in the bottom. Maintain storage containers and areas clean to protect utensils and equipment from cross contamination. Do not store soiled utensils with clean items. Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. **Knives/container were placed in 3 part sink to be cleaned.**

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - Left faucet of 3 part sink was leaking (at joint between 2 handles where neck of faucet meets the base). All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair the faucet in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code. **Kitchen Manager stated a new faucet has been purchased and will be installed in the near future**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - A) Floor drain below 3 part sink was soiled with buildup. B) Floor in dish area along walls/in corners was soiled with food/general debris. Clean the floor drains and floors throughout along walls/in corners daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - A) Ceiling vent covers throughout kitchen and above dish machine had dust buildup. B) Walls in dish area next to paper towel dispenser and below dish counter by chemicals had dust buildup. Clean walls and vent covers as needed to eliminate buildup of dust and other debris.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140(b) - Foods cooling in the walkin cooler were above 70F at 3:10pm when temperatures were checked and foods were pulled from the steam table at 1pm according to the labels on the products. Potato soup and sweet potatoes had internal temperatures of 114F-121F and 74F-80F respectively. Both products were discarded in the trash Roast beef that was also cooling was at 62F-65F. Plastic wrap was loosely wrapped with one corner uncovered for the roast beef to continue cooling properly. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F/below within an additional 4 hours - total cooling time 6 hours.  (See general comments)

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text: 750.830 - Dish machine sanitizing concentration registered at 0ppm chlorine. EcoLab was in for service on 1/30/12 and noted concentration at 75ppm. The dish machine log did not have any wash temperatures or sanitizing concentrations written down for today's date. Therefore it was not possible to know if the machine was properly sanitizing at any point during the day. Manager contacted EcoLab for service. The EcoLab repair person was in Decatur and said he would be able to come to the facility before the end of the day. Use the 3 part sink/quat sanitizer for any ware washing needs until the machine has been repaired and sanitizer is at proper concentration. Inspector will be back tomorrow morning for a follow-up inspection.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Raw shell eggs were stored above individual packaged pastries and fruit in the walkin cooler. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods. Shell eggs were moved to the bottom shelf below all ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - A) The drip guard of ice machine (closest to prep table) had some buildup on it. B) Inside the microwave had some dried food splash in it. Wash, rinse, and sanitize the above items between uses/as needed to eliminate buildup of mold, food, and other debris. **Ice machines get monthly service cleanings, but staff still need to clean/sanitize, as needed, the drip guards and other areas they can reach**

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - Clean knives were stored between the edge of the prep table and side of the knife holder. The edge of the prep table was soiled/sticky. Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. **As long as the area in question is maintained cleaned and sanitized the knives may be stored between the table edge and knife holder. The area has a large enough space to be cleaned/sanitized with ease.** Knives were placed in the knife holder slots.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed

The roll cart was moved, and the wet rag was placed in proper soiled rag storage area.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

Wash, rinse, and sanitize the above items and all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to eliminate buildup of dust, food, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) outside of pancake syrup bottle (dry storage); B) spice shelf above 3 compartment sink; C) sides of cooking equipment; D) hood filters; & E) inside tan garbage can (hallway on other side of dish room). Clean the above items and all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - Handsink in dish room was soiled. Handsinks, dispensers, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the handsinks daily/as needed to ensure employee hands are being properly washed and not potentially re-contaminated during handwashing process.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 & 1220 - A) Ceiling vent cover next to door of walkin cooler had dust buildup on it. B) Ceiling around oven exhaust pipe was in disrepair. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning. Clean the ceiling vent cover, and repair the ceiling around oven exhaust pipe. **A leak caused damage to the ceiling above the oven. Staff are aware of the issue, and it will be addressed during the current remodel.**

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text: 750.1300 - Spray bottle on lower shelf in dish room labeled alkaline bathroom cleaner/disinfectant had bleach in it. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances. Employee properly labeled the bottle during the inspection. **Make sure all chemical spray bottles are properly labeled as to their contents.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text: 750.1390 - Mop was observed stored with wet mop head down in the mop sink. Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored properly. Store mops hanging or inverted when they are not being used to allow for proper drying of mop heads. **Wet mop heads can serve as a food and water source for pests.**

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed several items in the walk in cooler without a proper label.  Label with the date and time all potentially hazardous food that you prepare requiring refrigeration at the time of preparation or storage.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed raw meat improperly thawing.  Properly thaw potentially hazardous food.  Corrected:  meat was placed in pans with cold water running over the meat, overflowing into the sink. 
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed the sanitizer concentration for the automatic dish machine at 0ppm.  Observed air bubbles in the dispensing line.  Corrected: The line was primed = 100ppm chlorine.  Maintain chlorine sanitizer concentration at 50 - 200 ppm for wash/rinse sanitize.
750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).
